newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar drifts lower in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar drifts lower in thin trading.

text.p: White sugar futures got off to a slow start on Thursday morning with little fresh fundamental news to prevent a gentle sideways drift, traders said.
By 1130 GMT all traded positions were marginally weaker and volume totalled a thin 133 lots. August was down 40 cents at $322.60 and October down by the same amount at $317.10.
Interest was scarce in August/October, which kept to its recent narrow value of around $5.50.
Traders said London still had room to the upside as the market moved into the summer, also voicing concern that world supply into 1998 could be on the tight side.
"People will buy the forward months because next year is looking a lot tighter that this year," said one. "But that's not to say in the meantime the nears will have some sort of washout."

Technical analysts said the fact that London had corrected lower after the rally seen earlier this month could signify that the longer-term uptrend could be resumed and that $330.80 resistance could be challenged.
Other traders said the raws market in New York was likely to set the pace in London until July expired on June 30, especially with the build-up of fund positions.
Trading was subdued in Paris with just 146 lots on the board, mostly August which was down 20 cents at $322.50. October was untraded.
